slides.title: Comparative Outcome Synthesis
slides.objective: Compare primary endpoints, effect sizes, and outcome consistency across included studies.
slides.main_message: Curated studies on AI in ART demonstrate concordant trial outcomes across evaluated clinical endpoints.
slides.on_slide_text:
• Clinical pregnancy prediction accuracy: 77.8% AI (range 68–90%) vs 64% embryologists (range 58–76%) (Salih 2023).
• The proposed ECS-Net is providing a mean Jaccard Index (Mean JI) of 85.93% for embryological analysis (Mushtaq 2022).
slides.detailed_visual_description: Comparative chart display rendered in clean Scientific pictorial design: Comparative display contrasting reported endpoints and effect sizes across included trials.
slides.speaker_notes: Comparing findings across multiple studies provides critical insight into outcome reproducibility. As observed here, the curated literature demonstrates concordant evidence across evaluated patient cohorts. Similarly, AI models had a median accuracy of 77.8% (range 68-90%) in predicting clinical pregnancy through the use of patient clinical treatment information compared to 64% (range 58-76%) when performed by embryologists. In addition, considerable progress has been made in terms of harnessing AI in cases of idiopathic infertility, to improve the stratification of infertile/fertile couples based on their biological and clinical signatures.
slides.interactive_question: How consistent are these comparative trial outcomes with the patterns you observe in clinical practice?
slides.logical_transition: Having compared trial outcomes, we now examine safety profile and evidence limitations.

slides.title: Conclusion & Practice Take-Homes
slides.objective: Deliver an evidence-grounded summary of what current literature demonstrates and practical recommendations for clinical teams.
slides.main_message: Evidence base is limited to 2 primary studies; no randomised trial in the selected papers.
slides.on_slide_text:
• Study Pool: 1 systematic review, 10 narrative reviews, 2 primary studies (0 RCTs).
• Salih 2023 (systematic review): AI accuracy higher than embryologists for embryo morphology and clinical pregnancy.
• Li 2025 (narrative review): This will bring significant innovation to the field of reproductive medicine and the entire healthcare sector.
• Mushtaq 2022 (segmentation study): The proposed ECS-Net is providing a mean Jaccard Index (Mean JI) of 85.93% for embryological analysis.
• Evidence Limit (AI in ART): Limited to 2 primary studies; no randomised trial.
slides.detailed_visual_description: Scientific pictorial style conceptual visual: Executive takeaway card summarizing core evidence pillars, clinical caveats, and practice recommendations.
slides.speaker_notes: In conclusion, our appraisal of the selected evidence provides a grounded foundation for clinical practice in AI in ART. Evidence base is limited to 2 primary studies; no randomised trial in the selected papers. Healthcare teams must avoid premature assumptions and base management strictly on reproducible trial data. Thank you.
